content: 1. When possible, reduce the dose of the medications being coadministered. If coadministration is necessary, evaluate for potential loss of therapeutic effect. Adjust the dose based on the prescribing information as needed. 2. Apomorphine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Arformoterol and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin base increases the effects of argatroban by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Aripiprazole and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Arsenic trioxide and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Artemether and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Artemether/lumefantrine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Asenapine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of atogepant by an unspecified mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended dose of atogepant with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 14. Atomoxetine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This increases the risk of atorvastatin toxicity, including myopathy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib. 18. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely and reduce the dose of axitinib as necessary. 19. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It may also decrease their levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin base decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 23. Erythromycin base and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 24. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of erythromycin base in accordance with its prescribing information. 25. Erythromycin base increases the effects of bemiparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin base decreases the effects of bendamustine by reducing its metabolism, leading to decreased conversion to active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of berotralstat by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of betrixaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the dose of betrixaban to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally once daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 29. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Erythromycin base increases the effects of bivalirudin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, bosentan decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Bosutinib increases the levels of erythromycin base by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Erythromycin base increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 36. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Buprenorphine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 40. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 41. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin base decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefoxitin, cefpodoxime, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 43. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dose of erythromycin base as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 44. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ceritinib and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
